entries.caption: Michael's Camino Portugués: Porto to Santiago via the Portuguese coastal, the Spiritual Variant, and a ferry transit across the Ría de Arousa. Roughly 310 km (193 miles).
Made it to Porto and secured my pilgrim passport and first stamps at Sé do Porto. Beautiful walk toward the ocean along the Douro River for a few miles until the jet lag set in.
A successful day one of walking. If you like ocean views, this Camino is for you — all day ocean. Just keep it on your left and you’re good to go toward Santiago.

This morning was 60 degrees and tomorrow starts in the upper 50s — I’m in heaven! A cool ocean breeze for most of the day, never broke a sweat until the last 5K which was a long hot march through farmland.

Well, today was different. We turned inland and walked through eucalyptus forests and hillside villages. Inland meant elevation gains though, so this was the most difficult day physically — probably the second hardest physical thing I’ve done behind only the ACI surgery and recovery. To cope I ate a whole pizza by myself 🤣

Today a shorter walk after yesterday’s effort. Near Viana do Castelo I went for a swim in these lovely man-made pools near the ocean. Water temp was probably mid-60s — it was warmer than the cold plunge at our gym — and I caught a little sunburn because I didn’t want to leave it.

My niece Ella Grace painted a rock for me to carry on this Camino. One side is a green dragonfly and the other an owl. After Zulu passed, I had an amazing encounter with a Barred Owl the next day, and an encounter with a dragonfly the day after Zola. I left the stone at the ocean in Portugal today, just south of Vila Praia de Âncora at a beautiful, secluded beach named Praia do Forte do Cão — Dog Fort Beach! — and got to say my signature goodbye to them one more time: “Bye girls, y’all be good, Mommy and Daddy be back later.”

This morning I crossed into Spain from Portugal at sunrise — and immediately lost an hour due to a time zone difference between the two countries. It was a long day with the most elevation gain yet, but a lovely walk through Galicia.

A difficult morning with lots of climbing. Views were 10/10 though. Finally some relief from elevation around lunchtime, when I descended into Baiona — a lovely beach town where news of the discovery of America by the first Europeans arrived in 1493. I swam at Praia América to celebrate this special connection to home 🇺🇸

Five days of swimming in a row! The water here is crystal clear and cold, so nice after a hot walk. I had a coffee at the beach next to a couple from Fort Worth, Texas, who just moved here two weeks ago and are in love with it so far, then ran into friends Mel and Katie for a swim at Praia do Tombo do Gato.

I left Vigo in the dark and climbed away from the sprawling city into the forests above and was treated to stunning vistas most of the day. It felt like a cold front came through which kept the temps in the 60s most of the day and very windy. Feet and knees hurt but my spirits remain well.

A real struggle today, mental and physical. Both feet and my right knee are absolutely wrecked. But I feel the pull of Santiago now, and should arrive there on Monday. To celebrate another completed stage, an impromptu Supper Club with Mel, Dominic, and Fabian.

After yesterday’s struggle I was dreading the walk today, especially after checking the elevation profile for this stage, which is my last 20+ km walking effort before Santiago. But instead of another suffer fest, I had a gentle, peaceful ramble over the mountain, through the forest, and along a babbling brook for much of the day, and a body that mostly cooperated. The Camino provides.
